"So that what is profitable and good may be yours," says Nicephorus, "it is open to you [?] to hear where and how this heresy, or rather apostasy, took its beginning and its progress, so that it may become well known that this accusation springs not from an imperial but from a Jewish way of thinking. For besides all the other heresies that were sown by the enemy and wickedly sprang up beside the Church of Christ, this bitter thorn also sprouted impiously alongside them. Thus it follows ranked with them, numbered the hundred and second after those listed before. It reads as follows: Heresy 102: Christianocategori, or Iconoclasts. They were called Accusers of Christians because they accused Christians, who worship one living and true God adored in Trinity, saying that they have worshipped as gods, just as the pagans do, the venerable icons of our Lord Jesus Christ, of our immaculate Lady the all-holy Mother of God, and of the saints. And as if they hated idols forsooth, they shamefully outraged the Church of Christ, overturning these icons and bitterly tormenting those who venerated them according to the custom handed down to Christians from the beginning. [?] and God-hated is this way of thinking. For some of the elders say that the heresy [?] sprang up thus. In Tiberias there was a certain man known to belong to the religion of the Jews and prominent among his nation, surnamed Tessarakontapechys, "Forty-Cubits" (otherwise Sarantapechys). He was an instrument of the wicked demon and had received him wholly into himself, and he practised sorcery and witchcraft as a kind of trade. This man was hostile to Christians and bore malice against the Church of Christ. He kept watching for an opportunity to attack and ruin true religion. He found his opening at that time, when the race of the Saracens was in power; their ruler was named Yezid. Ingratiating himself with him and, as one would expect, making a show of [?] concern, he foretold to him certain things to his liking. At the same time he promised that, if Yezid would follow his counsels, he would enjoy long life in his rule and would complete thirty years in it. Yezid, carried away by his own levity, since he embraced a dissolute life and gladly welcomed the prospect of its [?] being prolonged for a very long time, agreed to the impious man's proposal. It was this: that he should command, as quickly as possible, that every image set up in any way throughout his whole dominion, and in general the likeness of every living creature, be taken down and destroyed. Diabolical was the crime of the enemy of God, who hid his deceit so that, through the destruction of every likeness, the fair adornment of our sacred painting might also secretly be cast down. And when this unholy decree had been issued, the adornment of sacred images in the churches of Christ was immediately destroyed along with the other likenesses and statues. Some of these images they scraped off, others they obliterated with plaster. Some they even gave to the fire together with the holy buildings themselves, and their vessels and vestments; and these things were dared with profane and unholy hands. For those sent to do this compelled Jews and Saracens, who fight against Christ, to carry out the decrees. But Christians, though pressed and forced, could not be persuaded to lay hands on so great an outrage. From there the evil sprang up and grew, and burst riotously into the empire of the Romans. Nor was it ordinary people who received this corruption, but the very chiefs of the priesthood, called shepherds but proving to be wolves in their ways and their purpose. Among them was the bishop of Nacolea at that time. For by thinking and doing the same things as the enemies of God, they outraged the Church of God. What end [?] the introducer [?] of this [?] received, it would not be right to pass over. For that Yezid [lived?] no more than two years and six months

The hundred and third heresy: Aposchistae (Schismatics), also called Doxarii. Seeking their own glory, they do not submit to the righteousness of God or to his priests. Knowing the heresy of the Autoproscoptae, they seek the canonical rules; and though they are neither bishops nor leaders of the people, but some of the common herd, they separate themselves from the catholic Church. Emulating the Euchites, that is, the Messalians, they tell ascetics not to attend the church's assemblies but to be content with the prayers in their own hermitages. And they are in confusion, divided even among

themselves, for falsehood splits in many directions. Having departed from the communion of the Church, they make a show of strictness, each eager to prove himself better than the next. Some do not accept divine baptism, nor do they partake of divine communion. Others will not even kiss a newly made figure of the precious cross or a venerable icon. Thinking themselves superior to all people, and this is the worst of evils, they accept no priest at all. Instead, in the hypocrisy of liars, with their own conscience seared, they wrangle over words to no profit, storing up for themselves wood, hay and straw, fuel for the eternal fire. Let both the drunken violence of the iconoclasts and the madness of the Aposchistae be kept equally far from us: they are evils diametrically opposed, yet equal in impiety. The heresies set down above have been written in summary because they gave birth to the rest, since they number one hundred in all. The holy and catholic Church flees all of these as pits; made wise by the Holy Trinity, she teaches rightly and piously and cries aloud: We believe in the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, one Godhead in three hypostases, one will, one operation, and likewise in three persons: wisdom incorporeal, uncreated, immortal, incomprehensible, without beginning, unmoved, impassible, without quantity, without quality, ineffable, unchangeable, unalterable, uncircumscribed; equal in glory, equal in power, sharing one throne, equal in might, equal in nature; beyond being, beyond goodness, of threefold radiance, threefold sun, threefold brightness. Light is the Father, light the Son, light the Holy Spirit; wisdom is the Father, wisdom the Son, wisdom the Holy Spirit; one God and not three gods; one Lord, the Holy Trinity in three hypostases

…known: the Father is Father and unbegotten; the Son is Son, begotten and not unbegotten, for he is from the Father; the Holy Spirit is not begotten but proceeding, for he is from the Father. Nothing in it is created, nothing first or second, nothing lord or servant. It is a Unity and a Trinity, which was and is and will be for ever. It is understood and worshiped by faith, by faith and not by inquiry, nor by searching out, nor by demonstration. For the more it is searched, the more it is unknown, and the more it is pried into, the more it is hidden. So let God be worshiped by the faithful with words that do not pry. Believe that God exists in three hypostases; but how he exists is beyond the question "how." For God is incomprehensible. Do not say, "How is the Trinity a Trinity?" For the Trinity cannot be searched out. If you pry into God, first tell me about yourself and the things that concern you. How does your soul exist? Where does your mind move? How do you beget your word? How are you both mortal and immortal? If you do not know these things, which are within you, how do you not shudder to search out the things above the heavens? Think of the Father as a spring of life, begetting the Son like a river, and of the Holy Spirit as a sea; for the spring, the river and the sea are one nature. Think of the Father as a root, the Son as a branch, the Holy Spirit as fruit; for in the three there is one essence. The Father is the sun, having the Son as its ray and the Holy Spirit as its heat. Yet the Holy Trinity is far beyond every image and figure. When you hear of birth from the Father, do not think of a bodily birth; when you hear "Word," do not suppose a bodily word; when you hear "Spirit of God," do not think of wind and breath. Rather, glorify him by faith alone, without prying. For it is from his creatures that the Creator is understood by analogy. Believe and glorify the incarnate dispensation of the Son of God: that he was born of the holy Virgin without seed and inexpressibly, the same one being God and man without confusion and without change, who arranged all things for your sake; and render to him worship and service through good works. Venerate and honor the all-holy Theotokos and ever-virgin Mary as the true Mother of God, and all the saints as his servants. If you do this, you are a right-teaching worshiper of the holy and unconfused Trinity, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, the one Godhead, to whom be glory and honor and worship for ever and ever. Amen.
